sources.title: The Local Bubble Is a Magnetized, Multi-temperature Superbubble: 3D Dust Shell Model (A_G = 0.5 mag/kpc threshold)
sources.credit: O'Neill, T. J., Zucker, C., Goodman, A. A., & Edenhofer, G. (2024, ApJ 973, 136); Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/INB1RB
sources.citation: O'Neill, T. J., Zucker, C., Goodman, A. A., & Edenhofer, G. 2024, ApJ, 973, 136 (doi:10.3847/1538-4357/ad47b5)
sources.note: Derived from ONeill2024_LocalBubble_ShellProperties_A0.5.fits (786,432 HEALPix nside=256 directions derived from the Edenhofer et al. 2024 3D dust map). Aggregated onto a closed nside=48 HEALPix 2-manifold (27,648 vertices, 55,292 outward triangles) in heliocentric Galactic Cartesian coordinates scaled to 1 unit = 100 pc.

files.note: One Gaussian splat per vertex of local_bubble_oneill2024.glb (27,648; rows [x, y, z, r, g, b, sx, sy, sz, qx, qy, qz, qw, opacity], 1 unit = 100 pc), from the same O'Neill et al. (2024) shell table, averaged per HEALPix nside 48 cell over 19 to 36 rows. Measured: the centre (the mesh vertex, at the peak distance d, where the slab is centred), the orientation (the table's shell normal, turned outward), the thickness along the normal (the table's line-of-sight thickness times |n . r|, drawn as a uniform slab's sigma, width / sqrt(12)). Grid geometry, a presentation value: the footprint across the normal (the cell's side as a slab sigma). Presentation mapping of a measured quantity: opacity = 1 - 10^(-0.4 A_G), the fraction of G-band light the shell absorbs along the line of sight from the Sun. Simulated: the colour, one neutral grey for every splat; dust extinction is not emission, so no colour stands for an emission line.

The Moon at true scale on a 1 degree latitude-longitude grid: 361 x 181 = 65,341 vertices, 128,880 triangles, 2,865,384 bytes. Measured: each vertex's radius is 1727.4 km plus the mean LOLA height in the 1 degree box centred on it (at each pole, the mean of the half degree band), with no exaggeration; 10 units = 1737.4 km. SVS says this elevation map "was taken directly from the latest (as of spring 2019) gridded data products of the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter instrument team" and that the kit's maps "are designed for use in 3D rendering software". Conventions kept from the mesh this replaced: +y north, longitude 0 toward +x, 90 E toward -z, u = (longitude + 180) / 360, v = (90 - latitude) / 180. POSITION, NORMAL and TEXCOORD_0 only, no material or image.
